prerequisites: functions of one and more variables
Statics (construction of equations of statical equilibrium and free body diagrams)
Strength of materials I (stress and strain tensors, beam theory, limit states of ductile and brittle materials)

learning_outcomes.text: Extend knowledge on the possibilities of safety assessment of engineering structures.
Manage the analytical solutions of deformations and stresses in various bodies.
Extend knowledge on limit states, especially under the conditions of cyclic loading and existence of cracks in the body.

Be able to categorize common types of tasks of strength of materials and is able to choose an appropriate methodology of problem solution in the given circumstances via the corresponding analytical solution, preparation of input data for a numerical calculation or design of an experimental technique.
Be able to distinguish and assess the basic limit state of structures.

syllabus_topics: General strength of materials – basic quantities, system of relationships among them and generalized Hooke’s law
Basics of linear elastic fracture mechanics
Crack growth at static and cyclic loading
Fatigue strength of beams – concept of nominal stresses
Fatigue strength of beams – concept of local stresses and strains
Dividing into groups and assigning the tasks
Stress and strain states and generalized Hooke’s law
Hooke’s law at assessment of strain gauge measurements
Fatigue strength of beams – symmetric stress cycle
Fatigue strength of beams – asymmetric stress cycle
Fatigue strength of beams – combined and non-proportional loading

assessment_methods.method: Attendance and active participation in seminars, submission and presentation of given tasks
Written test (first mandatory part of examination)
Oral examination (optional second part of examination)

assessment_rules: To receive course-unit credit, attendance and active participation in seminars, and submission and presentation of given tasks are required, with a maximum of 10 points achievable. The examination consists of a mandatory written test worth a maximum of 80 points, and an optional oral examination with a score ranging from -10 to +10 points. Unexcused absence from seminars is grounds for not granting the course-unit credit.
